newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh group backs jute promotion.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh group backs jute promotion.

text.p: Efforts are being made to promote the use of jute, which faces stiff competition from synthetic materials that are cheaper and lighter, officials with the International Jute Organisation (IJO) said on Monday.
IJO executive director K.M. Rabbani told a news conference the group would seek assistance from donor nations for research and promotion. Jute is a plant fibre used for sacking, mats and cord.
"We are concentrating more on research to make the jute fibre finer and lighter," Rabbani said at the end of a three-day meeting of the organisation's governing council.
IJO officials said the group needed about $10 million to continue development activities aimed at promoting jute in Europe, where synthetics were especially popular.

"Our ultimate objective is to raise the demand for jute in the international market. But we are also concerned about the waning interest of farmers in producing jute which is less remunerative than other crops," Rabbani said.
Rabbani said the IJO wanted to provide farmers with higher-quality seeds for a higher yield. "The farmers' interest can be revived if we can make jute more remunerative than other crops," he said.
The Dhaka-based IJO comprises Bangladesh, India, China, Nepal and Thailand and 22 consuming nations, mostly in the West.
Bangladeshi officials said the country's annual jute exports had dropped to about $250 million from nearly $500 million in the 1970s.
Rabbani said world production of jute, extracted from a reed-like plant, dropped to 2.58 million tonnes in 1995/96 (July-June) from 3.4 million tonnes in 1991/92.
